subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters on the embedded attempt path, and what invalidation boundary should it use?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-backed, but cache placement affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the broader prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Land narrow internal cache
options.body: Refresh https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 or replace it with the same bounded cache shape for known safe bundled normalizers while preserving fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider/tool facts to avoid adding a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main live Google/Gemini or heap proof showing the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Land narrow internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 or replace it with the same bounded cache shape for known safe bundled normalizers while preserving fresh tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The cache decision intersects the prepared-runtime direction and provider/runtime boundary tracked by mcaxtr's maintainer-owned migration issue.
